extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners (attorneys/agents) and counsel involved in USPTO disciplinary matters
extracted.subtask_description: Final Order resolving disciplinary action against a USPTO-registered practitioner, setting forth stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and agreed sanctions (suspension, account dissociation, publication, waiver of appeal). Applies USPTO professional conduct rules and procedures for suspension/reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO jurisdiction for disciplinary proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over this matter pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19, 11.20, 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order invokes statutory and regulatory bases for authority to institute and approve discipline of registered practitioners before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is subject to the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct, 37 C.F.R. § 11.101 et seq.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registered practitioners before the USPTO must comply with the Office's Rules of Professional Conduct; violations can be the basis for discipline by the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification requirement after out-of-jurisdiction suspension (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(a), within 30 days of being suspended by another jurisdiction, a practitioner subject to the disciplinary jurisdiction of the Office shall notify the OED Director of the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely notice to the OED Director is mandatory; failure to notify within 30 days is a discrete procedural violation noted in the record (Respondent did not inform OED until a later date).

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation for being publicly disciplined by another jurisdiction (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent acknowledges that, based on the stipulated facts, Respondent violated 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h) of the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct by being publicly disciplined on ethical or professional misconduct grounds by the Supreme Court of the State of Oregon in In re Myers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public discipline by a state court for ethical/professional misconduct may constitute a basis for USPTO disciplinary action under § 11.804(h).

rubrics_metrics.name: State-court-found ethical violations as grounds for USPTO discipline (Oregon RPCs)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Oregon Supreme Court approved discipline for violations of Oregon Rules of Professional Conduct: RPC 1.3 (diligence), RPC 1.4(a) (communication), RPC 1.16(d) (declining/terminating representation — protect client's interests on termination), RPC 3.4(c) (fairness to opposing counsel — not knowingly disobey tribunal rules), RPC 8.1(a)(2) (disciplinary matters — failure to disclose or respond), and RPC 8.4(a)(4) (misconduct prejudicial to administration of justice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Findings of specific state RPC violations were used as factual/legal basis for the USPTO's disciplinary determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties of suspended or excluded practitioner (37 C.F.R. § 11.58)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent supplemented his response with an Affidavit setting forth his full compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners who are suspended or excluded must comply with the duties set out in § 11.58 (e.g., cease practice, protect clients' interests); representation of compliance can affect timing and imposition of sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanction: suspension from practice before the Office (term and commencement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended from practice before the Office for six (6) months; Respondent's six-month suspension shall commence nunc pro tunc on June 29, 2024 — the date Respondent provided a sworn declaration representing full compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office may impose a specified suspension period and may apply the suspension nunc pro tunc when a practitioner requests it and represents compliance with required duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on resuming practice until reinstated (37 C.F.R. § 11.60(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not resume practice of patent, trademark, or other non-patent law before the Office until a petition requesting Respondent's reinstatement to practice before the USPTO is granted as set forth in 37 C.F.R. § 11.60(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A suspended practitioner must obtain formal reinstatement under the procedures of § 11.60 before resuming practice before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from Customer Numbers and electronic accounts during suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent's name shall be dissociated from any Customer Number(s) and USPTO verified Electronic System account(s), and Respondent shall not apply for, obtain, nor have his/her name added a USPTO Customer Number or a USPTO verified Electronic system account unless and until he/she is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspended practitioners must be removed from or blocked from USPTO electronic accounts and customer numbers for the suspension duration, with reapplication only after reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order and Official Gazette notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order at the OED's electronic FOIA Reading Room and shall publish a notice in the Official Gazette that is materially consistent with the specified notice of suspension text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final disciplinary orders are published for public reading in the OED FOIA Reading Room and in the Official Gazette with specified content summarizing the discipline and authorities involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office may rely on disciplinary record in future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in this Final Order shall prevent the Office from considering the record of this disciplinary proceeding, including the Final Order: (1) when addressing any further complaint or evidence of the same or similar misconduct; (2) in any future disciplinary proceeding against Respondent (i) as an aggravating factor ... and/or (ii) to rebut any statement or representation by or on Respondent's behalf; and/or (3) in connection with any request for reconsideration pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A practitioner's disciplinary history may be used as aggravation, rebuttal, or evidentiary support in subsequent matters before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of rights to seek reconsideration, review, or appeal (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.56, 11.57)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent waives all rights to seek reconsideration of the Final Order under 37 C.F.R. § 11.56, waives the right to have the Final Order reviewed under 37 C.F.R. § 11.57, and waives the right otherwise to appeal or challenge the Final Order in any manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties may agree to waive procedural rights to reconsideration or review as part of a settlement that includes sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigating considerations in determining sanction
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent has acknowledged his ethical lapses, demonstrated genuine contrition, accepted responsibility for his acts and omissions, and cooperated with OED's investigation by providing informative, supplemental responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledgement of misconduct, contrition, acceptance of responsibility, and cooperation with investigation are cited as mitigating factors informing the agreed-upon sanction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs between parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Each party shall each bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of the Agreement and this Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement can include allocation of costs such that each party bears its own expenses related to the disciplinary matter and settlement implementation.
